explain.say: Wind is air on the move, and the Sun is its engine. Sunshine heats the Earth unevenly: land warms faster than sea, and the tropics get more sunlight than the poles.

faq.q: Why does air move from high to low pressure?
faq.a: Where air is packed more tightly it pushes harder, so it spreads towards places where it is pushing less, just like air rushing out of a pumped-up balloon. That movement is wind.
Low pressure is where there is a little less air pressing down, often because warm air is rising. It usually brings clouds and rain, because the rising air cools and its vapour condenses.
asks: What does low pressure mean in weather?

faq.q: Why does the Sun heat some places more?
faq.a: Near the equator sunlight hits the ground straight on, concentrating its energy, while near the poles it arrives at a low slant and spreads out. Land also heats up faster than water.
asks: Why is the equator hotter than the poles?

faq.a: Earth spins underneath moving air, which makes winds curve: to the right in the northern hemisphere and to the left in the southern. This is called the Coriolis effect.

faq.q: What is the fastest wind ever measured?
faq.a: Apart from tornadoes, the fastest gust measured by an instrument was 408 kilometres per hour, on Barrow Island, Australia, during Cyclone Olivia in 1996.
asks: What is the strongest wind on Earth?

facts: The fastest wind gust measured outside a tornado was 408 kilometres per hour, on Barrow Island, Australia, in 1996.
Wind strength is often described with the Beaufort scale, from 0 for calm to 12 for hurricane force.

quiz.why: Air spreads from where it presses harder, high pressure, to where it presses less, low pressure.

wrong.0: That is backwards: air moves away from high pressure, towards low pressure.
wrong.2: Winds blow from every direction, depending on where high and low pressure are.
